correctness.rationale: The finite-horizon count law is verified from the exchangeable missing set: intersection with an independent uniform q-subset has generating function binom(n,q)^(-1)e_q(1-r_i+r_i z). For Im z>0 the zeros in t of H_z(t)=product_i(t+1-r_i+r_i z) lie in the strict lower half-plane or at -1, whose convex hull excludes 0; repeated Gauss–Lucas gives zero-freeness of the required derivative and real nonpositive PGF zeros, hence a Poisson–binomial factorization. This concerns only the count, not missing-label independence. For fixed s, u=(1-s/n)^k, v=((n-s)(n-s-1)/(n(n-1)))^k yield Var Z=nu(1-u)+n(n-1)(v-u^2)~e^(-x)n^(1-alpha). The independent-Bernoulli normal Stein derivative bound yields W1<=2/sigma; the 1-Lipschitz distance from the standardized lattice gives (1/4-o(1))/sigma lower uniformly in lattice translation. Boundary packets s=0 or n in finite-horizon part; asymptotics fixed s>=1, 0<alpha<1, x real, n sufficiently large. Independently recomputed exact hypergeometric laws and real roots for small n and varying packets, corroboration only.

value.rationale: Unseen coupon counts under repeated fixed-size group drawings are a natural exchangeable dependent occupancy statistic. Their exact finite-horizon Poisson–binomial distribution is a structural theorem permitting independent-sum tools despite dependent indicators; the optimal two-sided normal W1 rate resolves the specific low-alpha optimality limitation explicitly identified by Betken–Thäle. The lattice lower bound matches the upper rate on the full alpha interval, not a routine finite check.

limitations: All normal approximations require a fixed positive packet size, fixed 0<alpha<1 and x, not a uniform endpoint theorem.
Finite packet structural theorem assumes packets independent and uniform of deterministic sizes; unseen-label indicators are dependent.
